root_idea.summary: The root centers on the number nine and the act of reaching or occupying the ninth position.
root_idea.development: From the cardinal number nine, the lexical field extends to becoming or making a group nine, taking a ninth part, ordinal uses, nine-day intervals, and named groups of three nights ending with the ninth night.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group contains the alternate cardinal form تِسْعٌ and the tens form تِسْعُونَ; both belong under the normalized numeral entry تِسْعَةٌ, with ninety represented as a separate Quranic sense.
تِسْعَةٌ is the supported classical citation form for the Quranic cardinal numeral.

senses.definition: The cardinal number nine; a quantity or group of nine.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic forms include تِسْعٌ and تِسْعَةٌ, distributed according to the grammatical gender of the counted noun. The same cardinal value occurs as the nine component in تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ, “ninety-nine,” and تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ, “nineteen.”

senses.definition: Ninety, the tens numeral formed with nine.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic surface form is تِسْعُونَ in the expression تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً, where it denotes ninety rather than nine in isolation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a ninth part of a people's possessions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use concerning division of property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become the ninth member of a group, or by joining it to make a group of eight into nine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use describing the subject's addition to an existing group.
A Form II causative use; this is distinct from the temporal idiom recorded below.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain nine nights with one's wife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional temporal use, which is also said to extend analogically to other actions or sayings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become nine, or to become ninety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied Form IV entry records the subject as reaching either of these numerical totals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be on a nine-day watering interval, of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The interval is described as nine days, with eight nights between waterings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ninth part; one of nine equal parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fractional noun distinct from the cardinal numeral.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ninth-day watering interval for camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A named interval in camel watering practice, counted as nine days or eight nights between waterings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The ninth young one or offspring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use for birth order.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A set of three nights of the lunar month ending with the ninth night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually the seventh, eighth, and ninth nights; one reported view applies the term to the first three nights instead.
An ordinal use distinct from the Quran-attested cardinal sense “ninety.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ninth; one who or that which makes a group of eight nine by joining it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinal and its underlying participial relation are recorded together; compounds such as تَاسِعَ عَشَرَ denote “nineteenth.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The tenth day of Muḥarram, or the day before ʿĀshūrāʾ according to the reported usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A post-classical or disputedly classical calendrical term, also reported as a name for the same day as ʿĀshūrāʾ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope consisting of nine strands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for a nine-stranded rope.

cautions: The supplied QAC grouping combines the cardinal forms تِسْعٌ and تِسْعَةٌ with the surface form تِسْعُونَ at 38:23; the latter is therefore represented explicitly as the Quranic sense “ninety.”
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:tsE:16677:g1:main records تُسَاعَ as potentially meaning “nine and nine” or “nine at a time,” but states that the form seems not to have been in use; it is retained as an unresolved lexical report rather than treated as an established meaning.
